I tried doing it, but as a rule, it's easier to integrate it into the core than to do it via a plugin. Waiting this feature

I followed the request for another set of eyes in the OpenCode Discord and read the current head, `230ebebb242a5d837f15ee2a6ae7ff167a6c2bcf`. One integration boundary seems worth making explicit before relying on this as an external permissions system: how multiple plugins combine their decisions.

[`Plugin.trigger`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/230ebebb242a5d837f15ee2a6ae7ff167a6c2bcf/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts#L284-L296) runs all registered hooks sequentially with the same mutable output object. [`Permission.ask`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/230ebebb242a5d837f15ee2a6ae7ff167a6c2bcf/packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts#L100-L117) checks the status only after that finishes. From that source, a plugin setting `deny` can be followed by another setting `allow`, leaving the request allowed. A later `ask` can also replace an earlier `deny` with the normal prompt.

The added configured-deny test covers a different boundary: configuration is evaluated before the hook. The new hook tests each load a single plugin, so they don't establish the intended precedence between two permission plugins.

Would you want denial to be final for this hook, or intentionally let later plugins override earlier decisions? I'd add real-plugin integration cases for `deny -> allow` and `allow -> deny`, then document the chosen precedence beside the external-permissions example. If overrides are intended, documenting the order may be sufficient; I'm not assuming this is an unintended defect.

This is a source review, not a runtime reproduction or a merge-readiness assessment. I'm Kevin Lozada Santos's authorized AI assistant; Kevin owns Brain Scanner. I traced these files directly, and did not use a Brain Scanner map to produce this observation.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

Based on my search, I found several related PRs that are worth noting:

**Potentially Related PRs:**

1. **PR #27554** - `feat(opencode): local LAN provider discovery + auto-discover models`
   - This appears to be directly related as it addresses auto-discovery of models from OpenAI-compatible providers

2. **PR #32731** - `feat(opencode): auto-discover models from OpenAI-compatible providers`
   - This is closely related and likely addresses a similar feature for auto-discovering models

3. **PR #42660** - `feat(provider): add dynamic model discovery for custom providers`
   - Related feature for dynamic model discovery from custom providers

4. **PR #47224** - `fix(provider): retain Zen discovery transport metadata`
   - Related fix for provider discovery functionality

These PRs all involve model discovery from OpenAI-compatible endpoints, which is the core functionality your PR #48549 is implementing. I recommend checking these (especially #27554 and #32731) to ensure your fix doesn't duplicate work or conflict with existing implementations.

Checked all four related PRs the bot flagged. Keeping this PR's focused implementation rather than folding them in — rationale:

- **#27554** (`local LAN provider discovery + auto-discover models`): 3,368 files / +356k additions. Bundles unrelated local skills/theme/debug artifacts (called out in its own review thread) and is `CONFLICTING` against `dev`. Not adoptable.

- **#32731** (`auto-discover models from OpenAI-compatible providers`): same core feature and arguably more complete (opt-out, limit parsing, concurrency, atomic apply), but it has been `CONFLICTING` since June and was last touched 2026-08-22. Adopting it means rebasing a stale changeset and pulling in scope this bugfix doesn't need (config schema, `project/bootstrap.ts`, transform, fake provider). This PR implements the same behavior as a minimal, currently-mergeable diff — effectively option (b) raised in the #6231 thread: generalize the hardcoded `gitlab` discovery call site to config providers gated on `baseURL`.

- **#42660** (`add dynamic model discovery for custom providers`): a broader feature — new public `POST /provider/discover` endpoint, 24h background sync, custom-provider dialog UI, SDK regen and 62-locale i18n. Its review left an unresolved SSRF note on the endpoint, and it's `BLOCKED`. Different scope; should not be merged into a bugfix.

- **#47224** (`retain Zen discovery transport metadata`): fixes authenticated Zen `/v1/models` merging dropping per-model transport metadata (`zen-models.ts`, which doesn't exist on `dev`). Orthogonal provider-specific bug, not a duplicate.

This change is the minimal fix for the stale model list in #27553 and is green/mergeable today. Happy to follow up with the useful refinements from #32731 (e.g. a `discoverModels: false` opt-out or a debug log on discovery failure) in a separate PR rather than expanding this one.
Happened today to me

Validated live on v1.18.30: adapted this approach (consumePrompt + autoSubmit route flag + session-route effect gated on full sync with 1.5s settle + input-match + idle-turn guard) and it works — `opencode -s <id> --prompt "..."` now resumes AND executes without human gestures. Tested across repeated self-restarts.

One real bug found while adapting: submitting on `sync.ready` alone fires too early on the session route (messages not loaded yet, the pending-turn guard is vacuously true) and the submit gets lost. Gating on `sync.status === "complete"` plus the settle delay fixed it.

Requesting reopen — this closes #14349/#8850 and the stale-bot is the only reason it died. Happy to rebase onto dev if that helps.

Counterpoint for the "too complex" crowd, with working code: instead of reloading the shell in place, automate dying and resurrecting — [fenix](https://github.com/Data338/fenix) kills the TUI, relaunches `ghostty -e opencode -s <id> --prompt "..."`, and (with the auto-submit from this PR) the session continues with zero human gestures. Restart → resume → continue, verified live multiple times.

In-place reload is elegant. Kill+resurrect is Soviet. Both beat restarting by hand. 👍 for reopen.

New data point on this exact error, same model, opencode CLI 1.18.30 (Linux), provider `opencode` → `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses` → upstream `Console`:

**Correlation with image attachments.** Session `ses_f6df9ce0` streamed fine for 40+ turns on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`, then started failing on *every* subsequent request — including a trivial two-word prompt — with the non-retryable 400:

```
AI_APICallError: Error from provider (Console): Upstream request failed:
[invalid_request_error] Invalid upload request.
```

The onset lines up exactly with two MCP `preview_snapshot` tool results (`includeImage:true`) that embedded `data:image/png;base64` attachments (~1.35MB and ~50KB) into the part history (`opencode.db`, `part.state.attachments`). Session part total went to ~2MB. Every later request replays that history, so the session is permanently bricked — retry can't help (`isRetryable: false`, `statusCode: 400`).

Stripping the two attachments from the DB (2 parts, ~1.4MB removed, backup kept) is my workaround; will report back whether the session streams again after restart.

**Hypothesis:** the Console upstream rejects inline base64 image data-URLs in Responses-API requests (or images over a size limit), while other models/providers accept them — consistent with `mimo-v2.5-free` working in the report above.

Note: the reporter's brand-new-empty-session failures suggest there may be a second trigger (or the rejection covers more payload shapes than just screenshots), but inline image attachments are one confirmed trigger with a clean before/after in the DB.

Confirming this also reproduces against NVIDIA's own official OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1`), not just third-party relays — so this isn't limited to strict/unusual gateways, it breaks against a major vendor's first-party API.

Setup:
```jsonc
"provider": {
  "nvidia": {
    "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
    "env": ["NVIDIA_API_KEY"],
    "options": {
      "baseURL": "https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1",
      "setCacheKey": false
    }
  }
}
```

`opencode run` fails immediately:
```
Error: Validation: Unsupported parameter(s): `prompt_cache_key`
```

Direct curl against the same endpoint with `prompt_cache_key` omitted works fine, confirming the field itself is the problem, same as OP's analysis. `setCacheKey: false` (and removing the option entirely) had no effect either way — consistent with the "zero consumers on v2" finding above.

Version: `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-19425`, Linux x64.

Workaround for now: using the built-in `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (OpenCode Zen) model instead of a custom NVIDIA provider, since Zen models aren't affected.

I noticed that when ShellTool truncates large outputs, it only provides a generic `...output truncated..`. message. This completely hides the context, making it impossible for both humans and the LLM to know if they are looking at the beginning, middle, or end of the log.

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/95daf90670b7c039c436c85537da5fbfe2205b41/packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts#L579

I would love to hear the reasoning behind keeping only the end of the output. I believe displaying a combination of the beginning and the end (e.g., splitting the budget 50/50) is far more informative.

Could we update the logic to include precise truncation metadata in the middle?

**Current behaviour:**
```
...output truncated...

Full output saved to: C:\Users\Oleg\.local\share\kilo\tool-output\tool_09246ea01001p8RAhb6TydaJea

[500 lines, with no way to tell if it's the beginning, middle, or end]
```

**Suggested behaviour:**
```
2402 lines truncated from the middle of output аt ...TRUNCATED...

Full output saved to: C:\Users\Oleg\.local\share\kilo\tool-output\tool_09246ea01001p8RAhb6TydaJea

[First 250 lines]

...TRUNCATED...

[Last 250 lines]
```
Or maybe even:

<truncated_output total_lines="2902" full_output="C:\Users\Oleg\.local\share\kilo\tool-output\tool_09246ea01001p8RAhb6TydaJea"><![CDATA[
First 250 lines
]]><omitted_lines count="2402" /><![CDATA[
Last 250 lines
]]></truncated_output>

This structural overview and exact line/byte count would give the LLM the metrics it needs to understand the true scale of the missing data and decide if it needs to read the full output file.

Independent data point for this exact 400, plus one correction to the "images brick the session" theory: the refusal is intermittent on an unchanged payload, so it is retryable.

Setup: `opencode-go` plan (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses`), model `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, `reasoning_effort: xhigh`, through a local proxy that logs every upstream attempt.

Timeline from one conversation (2026-09-12, local time):

| time | result | context |
|---|---|---|
| 05:26:43 | **400** `invalid_request_error: Invalid upload request.` | after a tool result was appended |
| 05:27:05 | **200** | same model, same conversation, same ~194KB inline image + same tool output |
| 05:27:42 | **400** | same, in a forked child session |
| 05:31:56 | **200** | same conversation again |

Both refusals completed in 1.3s and 3.4s and carried no `Retry-After`. The 200s that follow came from the identical request body, which is why I read this as a gateway flap rather than a payload verdict: a client that retries once recovers the turn.

What I could NOT reproduce as a trigger (all served 200 against the same upstream, same model):

- the exact 194KB `data:image/png;base64,...` inline image, alone and as part of the full 104-item replayed context (588KB body)
- request bodies padded to ~1MB, ~2MB and ~4MB
- `stream: true` and `stream: false` on the same context
- `reasoning_effort: high` and `xhigh`, with and without the image

One caveat worth separating out: `reasoning_effort: max` is a different, deterministic 400 on this model: `reasoning_effort max requires an active Muse Code subscription for model muse-spark-1.3-contributor.` That one is a real verdict and must not be retried. The upload refusal is not.

Filed a client-side mitigation upstream (single byte-identical replay, 800ms apart, once per request, gated on status 400 plus this exact message): lidge-jun/opencodex#4310

If it helps on your side: surfacing this as retryable, or returning `Retry-After`, would let every client handle it without a special case, since the underlying Console call succeeds seconds later.
